summary:
**LAST SIGNAL** is an educational, story-driven game that brings the history of NASA’s Mars exploration missions to life. Players take on missions inspired by three real robotic explorers: Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Through interactive gameplay, exploration, scientific data collection, challenges, and immersive visual and audio effects, players discover each machine’s achievements, challenges, and legacy.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming complex space exploration history into an engaging and accessible experience. Instead of simply reading facts, players learn by exploring Mars through the perspective of the machines that helped humanity understand the Red Planet.

LAST SIGNAL is important because it makes space science more exciting and understandable, especially for younger audiences. It also highlights the value of scientific discovery, engineering innovation, perseverance, and the contributions of robotic explorers—even after their missions come to an end.
details:
LAST SIGNAL is an interactive, story-driven educational game that lets players experience the challenges of exploring Mars through the perspective of three real NASA robotic explorers: Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity.

How it works:
Players begin by receiving a mission briefing from a fictional professor. They then explore a simulated Martian environment, move their robotic explorer, scan locations, and collect scientific data. Each mission introduces new challenges inspired by the history of the real machines. Visual effects such as dust storms, screen glitches, signal degradation, and emergency landing sequences, combined with sound effects and dialogue, make the experience more immersive. Completing one mission unlocks the next.

Benefits and intended impact:
The game makes space science and Mars exploration easier and more exciting to understand. It encourages curiosity about robotics, engineering, planetary science, and NASA missions. Our goal is to inspire young people to learn about space through interaction rather than reading facts alone.

Tools and technologies:
We developed a browser-based prototype using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used Canvas and CSS for graphics and animations, the Web Audio API for sound effects, and browser Speech Synthesis for character dialogue. The game runs in a modern web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

Creativity:
Our creative approach is to turn real mission histories into playable stories. Each rover or helicopter has its own visual identity, mission objectives, and challenges. Fictional cinematic scenes are used to make gameplay exciting while keeping historical facts separate from dramatization.

Team considerations:
We considered historical accuracy, educational value, accessibility, simple controls, engaging gameplay, and performance on ordinary computers. We also divided responsibilities across programming, game design, and NASA research and storytelling.
